title: How Teen ‘After-Prom’ Kings in LA Monetized the High School Rager
gist: MyPlots, an LA-founded ticketing app with over 1 million users and a 20% take rate on teen and young-adult party ticket sales, is raising a $10 million round and expanding into celebrity nightlife, operating in a compliance and liability gray zone where minors, alcohol, and informally-permitted venues intersect.

insights.claim: MyPlots, a party-ticketing app founded by Jack Schwartz that launched in January 2025 and targets under-21s in LA, has grown to more than 1 million users while taking a 20 percent cut of all ticket sales, an established, scalable take-rate model built around a demographic largely unaddressed by mainstream ticketing platforms.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: A concrete unit-economics figure (20% take rate, 1M+ users) for a niche ticketing platform serving an underserved, high-frequency-spending youth demographic.
insights.locator: MyPlots launched its namesake app in January 2025

insights.claim: Competitor Partiful, described by an industry promoter as the dominant event-promotion platform before MyPlots, announced in June 2026 that it would begin offering in-app ticketing, apparently in direct response to the feature that had originally differentiated MyPlots.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: MyPlots' core feature moat is already eroding as a larger incumbent copies its monetization mechanic, a competitive-dynamics signal relevant to the startup's fundraising narrative.
insights.locator: When it launched last year, the ticketing feature distinguished MyPlots

insights.claim: MyPlots is in the middle of raising $10 million from angel investors to establish a permanent office, hire a sales team to book talent for parties, and stage a planned 10,000-person festival on Santa Monica beach the following summer.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: Signals an intent to scale from a teen-party ticketing app into a full event-production and festival operator, a materially different (and more capital-intensive) business than its origin.
insights.locator: MyPlots is in the middle of a search for angel investors

insights.claim: MyPlots' nominal age requirement of 18 is functionally porous—the founder concedes 'people find ways around that'—and its integrated payment processor Stripe permits account holders as young as 13 if a parent is enrolled, an unresolved age-verification gap as the platform scales into paid, alcohol-adjacent nightlife.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: A structural compliance gap that exposes the platform to regulatory and payments-partner risk as its user base and event scale grow.
insights.locator: To use MyPlots, users technically need to be 18

insights.claim: An insurance broker states that once minors and alcohol combine at a venue, no carrier will knowingly provide coverage, and that minors generally cannot be held to contracts, meaning much of the underlying teen-party economy MyPlots facilitates operates on largely uninsurable and legally unenforceable footing.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: Highlights the tail-risk liability structure underlying the platform's core teen-event use case, relevant to assessing downside legal exposure for MyPlots and its promoters.
insights.quote: Take that same party and make everyone 21, and it’s insurable. Add minors and alcohol, and no carrier will knowingly touch it.
insights.locator: Here’s what it really comes down to

insights.claim: MyPlots' founder explicitly disclaims legal responsibility for events booked through the platform, stating he has 'no idea who 95 percent' of the promoters using his app are, positioning the company as a neutral ticketing intermediary while still marketing certain flagship events under its own brand.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: A liability-shifting platform structure similar to gig-economy intermediaries, offloading event risk onto individual promoters while the company still collects its transaction fee.
insights.quote: I have no idea who 95 percent of [the promoters] are
insights.locator: Schwartz wants to distance himself from promoters

insights.claim: MyPlots' 2025 'after-prom tour' relied on recruiting popular high school seniors, including cofounder Zane Harwin while he was still a student, as brand ambassadors to sell tickets to peers, a low-cost peer-network distribution model built on social status rather than paid advertising.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: An organic, near-zero-cost acquisition channel specific to closed high-school social networks, a growth mechanism that may not translate as the company expands to adult, celebrity-driven nightlife.
insights.locator: Their strategy for selling tickets was getting popular high school seniors

insights.claim: MyPlots has expanded from regional LA teen parties into celebrity-adjacent adult nightlife on the East Coast, including a $27,500 table-fee after-party for a Houston rapper's Madison Square Garden show and a prior Playboi Carti after-party, evidence of rapid upmarket migration into higher-revenue-per-event adult promotion.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: Indicates a deliberate strategy shift toward a higher-margin, higher-visibility adult nightlife segment as the company seeks growth capital and broader legitimacy.
insights.locator: Schwartz and the MyPlots team are hosting an after-party

insights.claim: MyPlots' founder Jack Schwartz says his eventual goal is to sell the company and start a new business 'something in AI,' indicating the current venture may be viewed internally as a stepping-stone rather than a long-term platform commitment.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: A founder's stated exit intent is a relevant signal for evaluating the long-term strategic commitment behind the company's current fundraising and expansion plans.
insights.locator: His ambitions go far beyond nightlife

insights.claim: A venue operator describes a recurring industry pattern where minors rent warehouses or office spaces and buy single-night event insurance for a couple hundred dollars on sites like Eventhelper.com or Eventsured, sometimes putting the policy under a parent's name to get around age restrictions.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: Suggests a broader underground teen-events economy exists beyond any single platform, one that could face regulatory scrutiny as it becomes more visible and monetized via apps like MyPlots.
insights.locator: Matt, a venue operator in his twenties

insights.claim: A Brentwood dance studio's floor broke under the weight of a crowd at a teen party rented by a promoter, sending 'rowdy rich kids spilling into the streets' according to a Los Angeles Magazine report, illustrating the physical safety tail-risk embedded in underinsured, informally-permitted venues used to scale teen events.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: A concrete, documented safety-failure incident underscoring real physical liability exposure in the teen-party venue ecosystem MyPlots and similar apps monetize.
insights.quote: rowdy rich kids spilling into the streets
insights.locator: Matt recalls that a dance studio in Brentwood

insights.claim: Multiple rival promoters and ticketing apps—310 Events, Off Campus Events, LA Social, Plots, and Turnt—already compete in the same youth-events monetization niche as MyPlots, indicating the category is a moderately crowded emerging sub-market rather than a single-winner opportunity.
insights.speaker: Manisha Krishnan
insights.so_what: Establishes competitive density in the teen/young-adult event-monetization space, relevant to assessing MyPlots' defensibility as it seeks growth funding.
insights.locator: In addition to MyPlots, there are promoters like 310 Events
